_metadata.description: Empirical business interruption loss magnitude distributions from NetDiligence ransomware claims data. Replaces duration-binned CSV outage table.
_metadata.source: NetDiligence Ransomware Spotlight 2024 (Table 5: SME, Table 6: Large Company)
_metadata.extracted_via: Substrata corpus (2026-05-08), records netd2024_ransomware_sme_bi_recovery and netd2024_ransomware_large_bi_recovery
_metadata.parameterization: Two-point lognormal: mu = ln(avg_usd), sigma = (ln(max_usd) - mu) / z_score. avg_usd used as median proxy (true median not reported). For max of N claims: z = invnorm(1 - 1/(2N)).
_metadata.duration_scaling: Sampled BI cost is scaled by (outage_hours / reference_duration_hours). Reference duration = 72 hours (3 days), approximately the median ransomware recovery time for SMEs. Linear scaling is the simplest defensible form given a single anchor point per revenue tier; nonlinear forms would require duration-stratified claim data that NetDiligence does not publish.
limitations: avg_usd used as median proxy — for heavy-tailed claims, mean > median, so this overestimates the center slightly
max_usd used as upper percentile — at N=294 this approximates p99.7 (z=2.75); at N=15, p96.7 (z=1.83)
No sector stratification available — NetDiligence BI data is not broken out by sector
Non-ransomware BI data not disaggregated by incident type in source

_design_note: Business interruption cost IS duration-driven (KB §04 compliant): revenue per hour lost, SLA penalties, emergency staffing all scale with outage length. This is the opposite of information-asset breach loss, where dwell time does NOT continuously scale magnitude. The duration scaling factor ensures that a 1-hour outage costs less than a 168-hour outage, proportionally to the reference duration.
